title: "Guide"

## Pipeline

Each stage is a class in `src/lowpoly_pdf_to_svg/`:

| Stage | Module | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Manifest | `config.py` | Reads the YAML: source PDF, sheet size, pages per cardstock. |
| Render | `render.py` | Renders each page with `pdftoppm` at 180 dpi; the PNG is kept in `data/<project>/previews/`. |
| Detect | `detect.py` | Separates grey cut lines, dashed folds and black edge numbers. The paper around the pieces is flood-filled from the page border; each enclosed area grows through everything the fill did not reach, so numbers and fold dashes touching a cut line cannot notch it. Outlines are low-poly: every edge is a straight line fitted to the printed cut line, corners are where edges meet. The right margin's "Print on … paper" note is read and checked against the YAML. Folds are found with a Hough transform, classified by line style (dash-dot or dashed; the `folds:` block in the YAML says which is mountain and which valley, Pepakura default dash-dot = mountain), and stretched into one straight line from cut edge to cut edge; a line that is not mostly printed dashes is dropped. |
| Read numbers | `ocr.py` | Tesseract reads each number; its confident reads train a digit matcher on the template's own font, which reads every number again. Every edge number is printed exactly twice, so uncertain reads prefer the candidate that completes a pair. |
| Edge pairs | `edges.py` | Links each number to the line it marks (a plain cut edge, or the fold of a glue tab) and pairs the two copies. Writes `edge-numbers.csv` and the summary `README.md` (the model folder's status page): a good pair is one tab and one plain edge of the same length. |
| Mirror twins | `symmetry.py` | Twins have the same faces; their glue tabs may differ. Face corners that sit 0.2–1.5 mm from their mirror corner move to the mirrored mean, or onto the twin when only the twin folded cleanly in the last 3D fold (up to 3 mm). A fold one twin lacks is added where the scan shows one. Mirror folds read in different styles both take the style the scan shows more clearly. Corners and folds edited by hand are left alone. Logged in `mirror-fixes.csv`. |
| Model | `model.py` | `Piece`, `Fold`, `Label` and `PageLayout`, in page pixels. |
| Write | `svg.py` | One Inkscape SVG for the whole project: document size in inches for Cricut Design Space, drawing coordinates in millimetres. |
| 3D fold | `fold3d.py`, `glueplan.py` | Folds the pattern back into the 3D model with `make -f fold3d.mk`. Glue is modular: by cardstock, then glue units of same-colour pieces tied by glues, then the joins between colours; `make -f fold3d.mk plan` lists them in seconds. See [3D fold-up](reference.qmd#d-fold-up). |
| Export | `export.py` | Last step, run with `make export` once review and fixes are done. Writes `<project>-export.svg` and the label key `<project>-labels.csv`. |

## Reviewing in Inkscape

`bowser.svg` needs Inkscape 1.2 or newer. Every PDF page is an Inkscape page at its true size (US Letter for this source), with one row of pages per cardstock. The layers are:

- **Source**: the rendered scans, locked and faint, to compare traces against.
- **Pieces**, with one sublayer per cardstock: each piece is one group named like `piece-04-03`, holding its `Cut` outline, `Score` folds (`Mountain folds` dash-dot blue, `Valley folds` dashed green) and `Draw` edge numbers as rotated text. The group carries `data-material` for later nesting.
- **Review** (hidden): artwork outside every piece, such as credits, instructions or an outline the detector could not close. Move anything that belongs to a piece into it.

Numbers the reader is unsure of are orange (`data-review="ocr"`), and their piece is labelled `⚠ check numbers`. On the Bowser template about 56% of numbers are read with confidence, and a spot check put those at roughly 90% correct; the orange ones are wrong more often. Folds that had to be stretched far to reach the cut have `data-review="unsnapped"` and the piece is labelled `⚠ check folds`. Search for either with Edit > Find.

The numbers are text, so you can correct one by double-clicking it. For the Cricut pen, turn them into single-stroke paths with Extensions > Text > Hershey Text before export. Before uploading to Design Space, delete the Source and Review layers, then assign Score to the fold paths and Draw/Pen to the number paths and attach them to each cut outline.

## Exporting for the Cricut

`make export` is the last step, after the review and `make fix` rounds. It reads the finished `<project>.svg` and `edge-numbers.csv` and writes `<project>-export.svg` beside them; the review file is not changed, so the check page, the fix loop and the 3D fold keep working on the PDF numbers.

- **Short labels.** Every glue pair gets its own two-character label, such as `2A`, in place of the PDF number, so the pen draws two characters instead of three. Both edges of a pair carry the same label and no other edge does; a number the edge check left unpaired gets a label of its own. The alphabet leaves out look-alikes (0/O, 1/I, Q) and 6/9, since labels sit at any angle, and every label has a letter so none reads as a PDF number; two characters cover 851 pairs, beyond that labels grow to three. `<project>-labels.csv` lists each label with its PDF number, edge status and pieces, and each label in the SVG keeps `data-pdf-number`.
- **Cardstock fill.** Each piece's cut outline is filled with the `color:` of its material in the YAML (named defaults for red, green, yellow, black and a few others when it is missing); holes stay open. Labels turn white on dark card.
- **Generated glue tabs.** The PDF's traced tabs (about 5.6 mm) are replaced by wider ones, 7.5 mm by default (half of a 15 mm double-sided tape, so one strip fits), with sloped ends. Each tab is laid onto the face of the partner piece it glues to and clipped to that face, 0.8 mm inside its other edges, so a tab never runs over a fold and never has to bend. Where two big pieces meet (both at least 5000 mm², glue edge at least 25 mm) and at stress points you list under `flaps:` (piece ids or PDF numbers, e.g. around the nose; a twin follows), the longest glue of the seam gets a square flap instead, like a paper doll's: 15 mm by 15 mm, one full tape width (as wide as the edge on a shorter one), centred on the edge, with only the corners trimmed that would cross a fold. Stress points are also found automatically from the folded 3D model (`fold3d.json`, `stress.py`): the mask rests on the head at its largest opening, each seam carries the paper hanging beyond it, and its stress is that weight times the sideways lever arm over the glued length squared, so horns, snout and other heavy parts on short seams score high. The top 10 % of seams (`stress_top`) get a flap. Bowser would get 49 flaps, 20 of them from stress. Mirror twins get mirrored tabs: the first twin's tab side decides for both. Where a piece glues to its own twin (the centre seam), the tabs alternate between the two pieces along the seam. A tab moved to the other piece takes its label with it. Pairs that are not one tab and one plain edge keep the traced tab, and so does any tab with no room. The pieces grow (Bowser: about 15 % more card), so re-nest after changing tabs. Set the sizes, or turn this off, under `tabs:` in the YAML; `--traced-tabs` keeps the PDF's tabs for one run.
- **Confirmed joins.** A PDF number can appear on more than two edges. List the right pair under `export: confirmed_joins:` in the YAML (`number`, the two `pieces`, optionally the `label` to keep); the export joins exactly those two edges, marks them ok, and the 3D fold glues them. A pair that does not resolve to one edge and one tab, or a label already in use, stops the export.
- **Frozen labels.** Once some cardstock is cut, `export: frozen_labels:` can point at a JSON file of the labels already cut (relative to the YAML); those pairs keep their label and new labels avoid them.
- **Piece numbers.** Every piece gets a number in its middle for finding it on the sheet. Mirror twins share one number, a circle on the left copy and a square on the right (left and right from the folded model); a piece without a twin gets an `A` prefix in a triangle. Numbers and labels are turned upright for the assembled model's vertical direction.
- Only the Pieces layer is kept, with its cardstock sublayers and each piece's Cut, Score and Draw groups; Source and Review are dropped and the review marks (orange numbers, `⚠ check` names) removed.
- The file follows the [export contract](export-contract.qmd) that the nester reads: piece id, material, colour, page provenance and the operation of every path are `data-*` attributes. `make export` checks it on every run.

For cutting the export on a Cricut (cut plan, Design Space operations, recut), see [Cutting on a Cricut](cricut.qmd).

## Re-cutting pieces from the 3D mesh (prototype)

`make segment MATERIAL=green` (or `PIECES=piece-11-04,piece-11-05`, twins added) cuts those pieces again from the folded 3D model (`fold3d.json`) instead of the PDF's split. The faces are welded into one mesh, made exactly mirror-symmetric (corners move about 1 mm; `--keep-shapes` skips this), and merged greedily, both twins at once. A merge is kept only if the piece still lies flat without overlapping itself and fits A4 with room for tabs. The score counts seams shorter than one 15 mm tape strip first, then tiny pieces (under 600 mm²), then pieces, seams, cuts inside a piece and seam length. A seam is one straight run, so a zigzag of short edges counts as several seams. Colour boundaries stay seams. The PDF's pieces are scored the same way for comparison. Output goes to `data/<project>/segment/`: `<name>-{pdf,new}-pieces.csv`, `-seams.csv` (length, short flag and load from `stress.py`), `-{pdf,new}.svg` (each piece flat: cuts solid, folds dashed, cuts inside a piece red) and `<name>.png` (both in 3D). `RESTARTS=n` adds randomised runs. Bowser's green goes from 26 pieces with 11 short seams to 10 pieces with 2 (both at the eyebrow, a colour boundary). The result is not yet wired into the export (issue #68).

`make partition MATERIAL=green` solves the same problem exactly over a pool of candidate pieces: every piece the greedy runs build, every single face, and each grown by one neighbouring face, all checked to lie flat and fit. A set-partitioning program picks pieces so each face is in exactly one and twins are picked together; each piece is credited with the seam cost of every edge it folds, which makes the score linear. HiGHS (SciPy) is the default; `SOLVER=gurobi` uses Gurobi (the free pip licence stops at 2000 candidates, about the nose). The answer is the best over the pool, and is kept only if it beats the greedy on the full score.

## 3D viewer and Piece Review {#viewer}

`app/fold3d-viewer.html` shows the folded model (`fold3d.json`) beside the flat pattern; picking a face in 3D shows that piece, cropped from its page when scans are available, and picking a piece in 2D lights up its faces. The models repository serves it with `make review MODEL=<model>` (local, with saving) and puts a read-only copy on its unlisted site with `make site`.

- **Cardstock** filter shows one material in both views; *Cardstock tint* sets how strongly faces take the card colour.
- **Labels** switches between the PDF numbers and the Cricut labels from the export (short glue labels and piece numbers, mirror twins sharing a number in a circle or square); *3D numbers* chooses which labels sit on the faces.
- **Find** takes a PDF glue number (the two pieces, glue edge in red), a Cricut label (the pieces carrying it) or a piece id (that piece and its twin); *Show all pages* goes back.
- **Issues** lists the pieces the fold flags for inspection (red: confirmed conflict, yellow: uncertain, green: reviewed and accepted); picking one marks the affected corners or edges in blue without changing the model.
- **Mirror pairs** steps through the twin pairs, worst first, with *Back*/*Next* (keys B and N); *Edit pair…* opens both in Piece Review.
- Right-click a face to *Edit piece in Piece Review…*, mark it as tab or surface (*Save tab marks & re-glue* writes the overrides and folds again), or *Recut this piece*; *Make recut* then runs `make recut` and opens the Cricut upload.
- The split between the two views can be dragged or collapsed to either side.
